a port's com-spec attributes, its data elements' policy and calibration access, its runnables'
symbols and the names the component states for its behaviour, events and access points. So an import
**without** `--update` that reported *unchanged* under 0.13.0 can now stop on a conflict: a
description that differs, a period that differed below a millisecond, a bound. An empty description
in the file is never a difference — it keeps the project's text, as described above — and a
component file 0.13.0 or earlier wrote carries none. A name the target states that equals the one
SWCraft would derive reads back from the file as stating none, so the target's own unchanged export is
reported as a difference; remove the stated name, which changes nothing in the generated file, or
import with `--update`. Still left out of the comparison, because a component file cannot carry them:
a value type's `unit`, a port's `measures`, the component's memory budget and the order of its ports.

A component whose types reach an implementation structure, array or pointer exports them with it,
each exactly as the whole-project ARXML writes it, and imports back into a project on this release.
So do the units, computation methods and data constraints its types name — each written once, at its
layer's package — and `swcraft import component` creates or reuses them as `swcraft import model`
does. One that the project already holds with another definition is refused, naming it: *shared
unit 'X' diverges from the target project's existing definition* (or *compu method*, *data
constraint*); one that differs only in its description is reused and listed under *Descriptions not
taken from the file*. A component that reaches an external element still cannot be exported on its
own, and no external element ever travels in a component file.

**A component file SWCraft 0.13.0 or earlier wrote may be refused**, the file named and nothing
written, in two cases:

- **It reaches an argument typed by an array.** The earlier writer stated `SERVER-ARGUMENT-IMPL-POLICY
  USE-ARGUMENT-TYPE` on every argument, which on an array-typed one — an `array` or an
  `implementation_array`, directly or through reference types — says the opposite of what SWCraft
  means and writes now (no policy, which the standard reads as the array's base type). The import
  reads that as a policy SWCraft does not carry, and such a line stops `swcraft import component`.
- **It states an initial value of an enumeration, or of an application type, the old way** — an
  enumeration's as a number, an application type's in the numerical form — where this release judges
  each value by the form the standard asks for (*An initial value is written in the form its type asks
  for*, above).

Its one false/false port API option per port does not stop it: each is one line under *Not carried
from the file*, and the component is imported — an option with a feature on is refused as before.

**The repair is to export the component again with this release** from the project that owns it, and
import that file. Where only the old file exists, import it with SWCraft 0.13.0 into a scratch
project, upgrade that project as *The model format changed* describes, and export it from there.

**A component file another tool wrote may now be refused** where 0.13.0 imported it: every piece of
behaviour content the importer does not read aborts the import, as described above, and so do a value
that changes what an RTE does and SWCraft does not carry (an operation's possible errors, an
application error, a com-spec attribute, a disabled mode, an argument policy), a description the
model cannot hold, a behaviour's or a runnable's own documentation, a runnable named like an event its
component generates, two names in one name space that differ only in case or sit in two lists, and two
spellings of one name in one package of the file. What only documents — a value's label, an element's
other documentation, its `UUID`, a package's own content, a name SWCraft generates itself — is printed
under *Not carried from the file* and does not stop it. A file that states the component's
`HANDLE-TERMINATION-AND-RESTART` sets `handle_termination_and_restart`; `--update` from a file that
does not state it keeps the project's value. A file that states none imports without it, and the
component is then reported until you set it.

**A component file this release writes places an element in a sub-package when the model says so**,
and a project on this release keeps that placement on import; the packages SWCraft writes into are
otherwise the same for every component, so a component exported from a project that sets no
`package` places nothing. Its data types, units, computation methods, data constraints and mapping
sets are written into their layers' packages under `/DataTypes`, so a component file differs from
0.13.0's in every path that names one. `--all-components` writes a component whose name differs from
another's only in case to `<name>~1.arxml` (above) where 0.13.0 wrote neither, and `--component`
without `--output` writes that component to the same file; every other file keeps its name.
`--update` keeps the project component's own `package`, a component's, port's or runnable's
description when the file carries none, and a shared type's or interface's description, which is
listed under *Descriptions not taken from the file*.

### If you script around the assistant's server

**The short model description leaves out a `false` it does not need to say — a breaking change for
a script that reads it.** When the server describes the model in its default short form (`discover`
with no `form`, or `form: "summary"`), a field no longer carries `required: false` or
`immutable: false`, and a layer no longer carries `optional: false`. A missing key means `false`:
a field with no `required` key is not required, one with no `immutable` key is not immutable, and a
layer with no `optional` key is not optional. Every `true` is still there, and so is every other
`false` (a missing layer still says `present: false`). The full form (`form: "full"`) is unchanged
and carries every one of the three. A script that reads `descriptor["required"]` from the short
form now fails on a key that is not there: read a missing key as `false`, or ask for the full form.
The server has no version switch for the old shape.

**The data types are four layers and three element layers.** The server addresses the model by
layer, and `data_types` is no longer one of them: a request names `application_types`,
`implementation_types`, `base_types` or `mapping_sets`, and the shared units, computation methods and
data constraints are the layers `units`, `compu_methods` and `data_constraints`. `discover` lists
fifteen layers where 0.13.0 listed ten. A change set's delta lists the type layers in the order
application, implementation, base, with mapping sets after them. A request that names `data_types` is
refused like any other unknown layer. The same thirteen tools reach every layer; no layer has a tool
of its own.

The model description the server publishes is larger: fifty-eight element kinds where 0.13.0
described forty, and 295 fields where it described 170 — among them the external elements, the
implementation structures, arrays and pointers, the shared units, computation methods and data
constraints, the operation events and `concurrent`, `handle_termination_and_restart`, the member
descriptions, the `package` fields, `is_service`, a data element's implementation policy and
calibration access, a port's `com_specs`, a timing event's disabled modes, a runnable's `symbol`, the
stated names, an external interface's member lists and a conversion's scale limits. Its default
short form is 59 870 bytes, where 0.13.0's was 45 614: the change above gave back more than eight
thousand bytes, and the new layers and fields took all of them and more.
A runnable read in the full form now carries `concurrent`,
`false` unless it is set; a port carries `com_specs` and a timing event `disabled_modes`, empty unless
set, an interface `is_service`, and a data element `sw_impl_policy` and `sw_calibration_access`,
`null` unless set. The compatibility question answers *not judged: external interface* for a pair it
cannot decide across an external interface, still with `ok: true`, because `swcraft check-model`
accepts that pair; two ports on the same external interface still answer `ok: true` with an empty
reason. A pair with an end on an external component's port answers `ok: true` with a reason
beginning *not judged: external component*, having compared the two directions and nothing else.

**An external interface's member lists come with it.** A read of an external interface carries its
`operations` or `data_elements`; a read that slices one member collection across a layer skips
external interfaces, whose lists hold names rather than members, and answers empty where only they
hold the name — it is not refused.

**The short form now carries every reference to another element, and leaves out one that is not
set.** When the server answers a read in its default short form, a port shows its `name`, its
`direction`, its `interface` and how many `measures` it has; a connector shows its `composition`, a
connector end its component or its composition, and a composition member its component type or its
sub-composition — the last four were missing from the short form before this release. A reference
that is not set is **left out** rather than sent as `null`: a port of an external component, which
names no interface, has no `interface` key in the short form, while the full form still shows
`interface: null` and the importer's `observed_interface` hint. A script should read a missing key
there as *not set*.

The short form is larger as a result. On a large model the short form of
the connectors grows, and the
ports of the widest components may no longer fit in one answer in the short
form either: the server refuses that read and offers the identities alone or a first page of 50,
which does fit. A script that read a large component's ports in one call should page them.

*Redacted 2026-11-13 for the open copy: statements about the real tool exports the maintainer holds privately (their names, number, figures and per-export results, also where a statement was phrased as an import of one of them) were removed; the release itself is unchanged.*
